_note: AI-drafted Call to Worship — pending Wilson's curation.

registers.label: Spare
lines: Three strangers came to Abraham's tent, and he ran to meet them.
God comes to us, and we will not turn away.
Sarah laughed at a promise too good to be true.
Is anything too wonderful for the Lord?
The harvest is plentiful, the laborers few.
Send us out; we are willing to go.
Come, let us worship the God who keeps his word.
We come, and we are sent. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Stand with Abraham in the heat of the day and look up — the fields stretch out, heavy and golden, ready.
Lord of the harvest, send us out.
At the tent he set bread and meat before strangers, and the strangers carried a promise that made Sarah laugh.
Lord of the harvest, send us out.
Jesus looks over the crowds, harassed and helpless, like sheep without a shepherd, and his heart breaks for them.
Lord of the harvest, send us out.
So he calls us by name and hands us the work: heal, proclaim, give freely what you have freely received.
Lord of the harvest, send us out. Here we are; send us!

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: Abraham ran to welcome the strangers at his tent.
Lord of the harvest, send us out.
They carried a promise that set Sarah laughing.
Lord of the harvest, send us out.
Jesus sees the crowds like sheep without a shepherd.
Lord of the harvest, send us out.
Come, let us worship, then go where we are sent.
Lord of the harvest, send us out. Amen.
